Dos billetes sintéticos: 20 Colones en Tyvek® (1983) y 1.000 Colones en polímero (2011)

Contexto Histórico y de Emisión

Un experimento previo al polímero moderno: mucho antes de la adopción generalizada del sustrato Guardian®, Costa Rica ensayó el Tyvek® —un polietileno sintético de alta densidad desarrollado por DuPont— como alternativa al papel tradicional, en el mismo período experimental en que Haití e Isla de Man probaron el mismo material.2

Un fracaso técnico instructivo: el Tyvek® resultó poco apto para la circulación en climas tropicales húmedos: la tinta no se adhería adecuadamente a su superficie no porosa, lo que llevó a un retiro acelerado de estos billetes y explica su actual rareza entre coleccionistas.

Detalles Clave Visibles en el Billete

  • Anverso: retrato de Cleto González Víquez, expresidente de Costa Rica, junto a la viñeta de su casa natal en Barva, con la leyenda “Barva, cuna del prócer”.
  • Reverso: ilustración detallada de la alegoría clásica de la Justicia, rodeada de figuras civiles.
  • Grabado en talla dulce: ejecutado por American Bank Note Company, con el relieve de tinta característico de esta casa impresora, adaptado experimentalmente al sustrato de Tyvek®.
  • Colorido: anverso en tonos sepia con motivos de palmeras a la derecha; reverso en tinta roja sobre la ilustración alegórica.

Mil Colones · 2011

Serie A · Braulio Carrillo Colina · Bosque Seco

Impresor Note Printing Australia (NPA), Melbourne
Serie / Fecha de Emisión Serie A, fecha base de diseño 2009, emitido a partir de 2011 (Acuerdo de la Junta Directiva N.° 11)
Referencia de Catálogo Pick-274a

Contexto Histórico y de Emisión

Del Tyvek® al polímero moderno: casi tres décadas después del experimento fallido de Tyvek®, Costa Rica adoptó el polímero laminado Guardian® para su familia de billetes de 2009–2011, impreso por Note Printing Australia —la misma tecnología usada por Chile, Malasia y Brunéi, con mejor resistencia y adherencia de tinta que el sustrato experimental de los años ochenta.

Detalles Clave Visibles en el Billete

  • Anverso: retrato de Braulio Carrillo Colina, junto al escudo histórico del Estado de Costa Rica de 1840.
  • Reverso: paisaje del ecosistema Bosque Seco, con un venado cola blanca y un árbol de guanacaste, árbol nacional de Costa Rica.
  • Doble ventana transparente: dos aperturas totalmente transparentes en el sustrato, una con la silueta del país y otra con un retrato en relieve óptico.
  • Numeración correlativa: par consecutivo con números de serie A005341238 y A005341239, indicativo de billetes sin circular conservados en secuencia.
  • Colorido: tonos rojo y magenta predominantes, con subimpreso rosado en ambas caras.

Notas

1. Wikipedia, “Polymer banknote”: “DuPont Tyvek polymer notes were experimentally issued by Haiti, Costa Rica, and The Isle of Man, from 1982.”

2. Ídem: el Tyvek® de DuPont fue un experimento temprano previo al desarrollo del polímero Guardian® moderno, con circulación limitada por sus limitaciones técnicas en climas húmedos.

World Polymer Banknotes · Costa Rica

Central Bank of Costa Rica

Two synthetic banknotes: 20 Colones in Tyvek® (1983) and 1,000 Colones in polymer (2011)

Obverse (top) and reverse (bottom) — Notofilia.com Collection

Twenty Colones · 1983

Series Z · Experimental Tyvek® · Cleto González Víquez

Country Costa Rica
Issuing Entity Central Bank of Costa Rica
Denomination Twenty Colones
Material Tyvek® — DuPont experimental synthetic polyethylene, not conventional laminated polymer1
Printer American Bank Note Company (ABNC)
Series / Date of Issue Series Z, Board Resolution No.° 6, June 28, 1983
Signatures Executive President · Manager
Rarity A piece of high numismatic rarity; rapidly withdrawn because the ink lost adhesion to the plastic substrate while circulating in a tropical climate
Catalog Reference Pick-252a (regular-circulation Series Z)

Historical and Issue Context

An experiment predating modern polymer:Long before the widespread adoption of the Guardian® substrate, Costa Rica tested Tyvek® —a high-density synthetic polyethylene developed by DuPont— as an alternative to traditional paper, in the same experimental period in which Haiti and the Isle of Man tested the same material.2

An instructive technical failure:Tyvek® proved unsuitable for circulation in humid tropical climates: the ink did not adhere properly to its non-porous surface, which led to an accelerated withdrawal of these bills and explains their current rarity among collectors.

Key Details Visible on the Banknote

  • Obverse:portrait of Cleto González Víquez, former president of Costa Rica, alongside a vignette of his birthplace in Barva, with the inscription “Barva, cuna del prócer”.
  • Reverse:Detailed illustration of the classic allegory of Justice, surrounded by civil figures.
  • Intaglio engraving:executed by American Bank Note Company, with the ink relief characteristic of this printing house, experimentally adapted to the Tyvek substrate®.
  • Color:obverse in sepia tones with palm tree motifs on the right; reverse in red ink on the allegorical illustration.

Thousand Colones · 2011

Series A · Braulio Carrillo Colina · Dry Forest

Obverse (top) and reverse (bottom) — Notofilia.com Collection
Country Costa Rica
Issuing Entity Central Bank of Costa Rica
Denomination Thousand Colones
Material Pure polymer — polypropylene Guardian® substrate
Printer Note Printing Australia (NPA), Melbourne
Series / Date of Issue Series A, base design date 2009, issued beginning in 2011 (Board Resolution No.° 11)
Catalog Reference Pick-274a

Historical and Issue Context

From Tyvek® to modern polymer:Almost three decades after the failed Tyvek experiment®, Costa Rica adopted Guardian laminated polymer® for its 2009 banknote family–2011, printed by Note Printing Australia —the same technology used by Chile, Malaysia and Brunei, with better resistance and ink adhesion than the experimental substrate of the eighties.

Key Details Visible on the Banknote

  • Obverse:portrait of Braulio Carrillo Colina alongside the historic 1840 coat of arms of the State of Costa Rica.
  • Reverse:landscape of the Dry Forest ecosystem, with a white-tailed deer and a guanacaste tree, the national tree of Costa Rica.
  • Double transparent window:two completely transparent openings in the substrate, one with the silhouette of the country and another with a portrait in optical relief.
  • Correlative numbering:consecutive pair with serial numbers A005341238 and A005341239, indicative of uncirculated banknotes preserved in sequence.
  • Color:predominantly red and magenta tones, with pink underprinting on both sides.

Notes

1. Wikipedia, “Polymer banknote”: “DuPont Tyvek polymer notes were experimentally issued by Haiti, Costa Rica, and The Isle of Man, from 1982.”

2. Ditto: DuPont's Tyvek® was an early experiment prior to the development of the modern Guardian® polymer, with limited circulation due to its technical limitations in humid climates.
